name: Specimen Sheet
description: The birds and wildlife around the panel, cut out and packed onto one printed page, each as large as the page allows. From BirdNET-Go (what the microphone heard, over a window you pick), iNaturalist (what people found nearby lately) or GBIF (what is recorded here in this month of the year). Classic plates and the records' own photos, or AI paintings in twelve styles or one you build; a demo garden until BirdNET-Go is set up.

cell_options.name: source
cell_options.label: Source
cell_options.help: BirdNET-Go is what the microphone heard, over the window you pick. iNaturalist is what people have found near a place lately. GBIF is what has been recorded near a place in this month of the year (it lags by weeks, so it is seasonal, not news).

cell_options.name: url
cell_options.label: BirdNET-Go address
cell_options.help: Where BirdNET-Go's web page opens, for example http://birdnet.local:8080. Leave empty for a demo garden based on this cell's location.

cell_options.name: window
cell_options.label: Window
cell_options.help: Which detections make the page, as Fugleramme groups them. Today is BirdNET-Go's day as it fills, with its hours. Last week is the last seven days by date. The rolling windows count back from now: under a day off BirdNET-Go's newest detections, longer from its species summary, keeping only the birds last heard inside the window. The demo garden keeps only to-day.

cell_options.name: location
cell_options.label: Place
cell_options.help: For iNaturalist and GBIF, the place to look around. For BirdNET-Go, the clock, sunrise and sunset, and which demo garden. Falls back to the app-level location, so BirdNET-Go with an address can leave it empty.

cell_options.name: radius_km
cell_options.label: Within
cell_options.help: How far round the place to look.

cell_options.name: kinds_inat
cell_options.label: What to show
cell_options.help: Kinds add up: Insects and Orchids together shows both. Nothing ticked shows everything.

cell_options.name: kinds_gbif
cell_options.label: What to show
cell_options.help: Kinds add up. Nothing ticked shows everything.

cell_options.name: days
cell_options.label: Window
cell_options.help: How far back iNaturalist's observations go.

cell_options.name: count
cell_options.label: How many
cell_options.help: Specimens on the sheet, picked by Which species. The more there are, the smaller each is; Scale can shrink the whole arrangement further.

cell_options.name: layout
cell_options.label: Layout
cell_options.help: A cluster packed from the middle out, each specimen as large as the page allows; a grid with a cell each; a hero: one specimen alone, with the others named beneath; or the year list: every species the sheet has shown this year, the earliest arrivals first, to-day's in ink.

cell_options.name: hero_bird
cell_options.label: Which specimen
cell_options.help: The one the hero shows. The first by Which species, as before; or Fugleramme's single plates: the bird heard last, or the newest arrival (of the window's birds, the one first heard most lately in the station's whole record, with the day it arrived); or the most heard, or the rarest, in the window.

cell_options.name: hero_note
cell_options.label: A note beneath
cell_options.help: A sentence or two on the species from Wikipedia, under the picture.

cell_options.name: hero_frame
cell_options.label: Around the specimen
cell_options.help: The painted backdrop asks fal.ai for a plate of its own: the specimen large on a patterned or foliate ground within an ornamental border, in the style chosen, shown whole. One painting per species and style; needs AI paintings on.

choices.label: An ornate rule frame, drawn on the page
An ornate backdrop painted in the style (AI paintings)

cell_options.name: spotlight
cell_options.label: Spotlight the latest bird
cell_options.help: As Fugleramme does: the bird heard last held large in the middle of the page, at six tenths of its short side, with its name larger, and the rest packed round it. Any packing.

cell_options.name: packing
cell_options.label: Packing
cell_options.help: How the cluster is packed. Balanced packs from the middle and then grows each specimen into the room left. Spiral and Voids are Fugleramme's packers: Spiral sets each specimen, largest first, on the first free spot out from the middle, for a round cluster; Voids sets each on the emptiest paper it fits, so the sheet fills to the corners.

choices.label: Balanced: grown to fill the page

cell_options.name: pictures
cell_options.label: Pictures
cell_options.help: Plates and photos cost nothing. AI paintings paint each species once, from a photo of it, in the style below, on white paper so the cut-out is clean, at about US$0.04 a species; the sheet shows plates and photos until each painting lands. Needs a fal.ai key in this widget's settings.

cell_options.name: style
cell_options.label: Style
cell_options.help: The style every painting is made in. Build my own composes one from the picks below and your own words; each combination is a style of its own, painted once per species and kept.

cell_options.name: build_extra
cell_options.label: Your own words
cell_options.help: Optional words added to the style, for example: with a little gold leaf on the wing edges. The bird is always painted alone with its perch, with no background.

cell_options.name: order
cell_options.label: Which species, when there are more
cell_options.help: Fugleramme's rankings, and the order of the sheet: the most calls (observations, records) in the window; the fewest in the window; the fewest in the station's whole record (BirdNET-Go; elsewhere the fewest days in this widget's own log); the latest heard or seen; or a mix that changes each day.

cell_options.name: marks
cell_options.label: Marks
cell_options.help: A small mark on a specimen: new, for a species new here or back after an absence; rare, for one on the sheet on few of the days the widget has logged (one in twenty at most, once it has logged a fortnight).

cell_options.name: labels
cell_options.label: Labels
cell_options.help: Captions under each specimen, or the page alone. A small cell carries the name only, or none, so the specimens keep their size.

cell_options.name: label_lines
cell_options.label: Label lines
cell_options.help: In this order. The count says calls, observations or records to suit the source; with BirdNET-Go it says when each was last heard. Last seen and the observer are for iNaturalist and GBIF; new or returning for BirdNET-Go.

cell_options.name: tally
cell_options.label: Count as
cell_options.help: The count in the caption as figures, or as tally strokes in fives.

choices.label: True to life: a crow large, a wren small
Close to life, narrower: the page packs tighter

cell_options.name: scale
cell_options.label: Scale
cell_options.help: How big the specimens are. 100% runs the arrangement out to the margins. Less packs it into the middle of the page with more paper round it. More makes each one bigger by showing fewer of them, the first by Which species: 200% shows about a quarter as many.

cell_options.name: panel
cell_options.label: Panel
cell_options.help: What the panel can show. Pictures are converted and contrast-stretched to match; on black and white the type is thickened.

cell_options.name: header
cell_options.label: Title line
cell_options.help: Where the title line (the place, the period and the date) goes. Below or hidden gives the specimens the room.

cell_options.name: title
cell_options.label: Title
cell_options.help: Blank uses the garden, the place or the username.

cell_options.name: exclude
cell_options.label: Leave out
cell_options.help: Species to leave off the sheet, one per line: a common or scientific name, a genus (Columba drops every pigeon in it), a kind (Insecta, insects, Birds) or a pattern such as *gull. An excluded species frees its place for the next. Case and accents don't matter.

cell_options.name: min_confidence
cell_options.label: Minimum confidence
cell_options.help: Detections BirdNET is less sure of than this are left out.

cell_options.name: names
cell_options.label: Bird names
cell_options.help: Common names come from BirdNET-Go in whatever language it is set to. Pick a language to take them from iNaturalist instead; they are looked up once per bird and kept.

cell_options.name: names_place
cell_options.label: Names as used in
cell_options.help: Prefers the names used in this country, where iNaturalist has them.

cell_options.name: night
cell_options.label: After dark
cell_options.help: Uses sunrise and sunset for the cell's (or the app's) location. Asleep shows the moon and the last bird heard once nothing has called for 90 minutes after dark. Night birds keeps only the birds heard since sunset on the sheet after dark.

choices.label: The garden asleep when it goes quiet
Only the night's birds after dark

cell_options.name: day_pages
cell_options.label: Dawn and dusk
cell_options.help: From an hour before sunrise to two and a half after, a dawn chorus page: the morning's birds in the order they started, with sunrise and the first song. From an hour before sunset to an hour after, an evening page: the last songs, latest first. Uses the cell's (or the app's) location. Reads only the birds heard to-day.

cell_options.name: quality
cell_options.label: Observations
cell_options.help: Research grade is where the community agrees on the species. Any takes every observation with a species, agreed or not.

cell_options.name: user_login
cell_options.label: Only this iNaturalist user
cell_options.help: Optional. An iNaturalist username. Set it to your own to see what you have catalogued, near the place or, with no place, anywhere.

cell_options.name: token
cell_options.label: Bearer token
cell_options.help: Normally blank. BirdNET-Go's reads need no login, even with Basic Authentication on. Fill this only for a reverse proxy or build that wants a bearer token.

cell_options.name: model
cell_options.label: Model
cell_options.help: All on fal.ai, all painting from a photo of the species. Nano Banana is faithful and cheap; Nano Banana Pro follows an unusual instruction better and draws finer detail; FLUX.1 Kontext Pro adheres most strongly to a style; GPT Image 2 is a good likeness with a narrower range; Seedream 4 is the budget one. Each model keeps its own paintings, so switching never throws any away. Left on Nano Banana, the ink-and-wash and stained-glass styles are painted with GPT Image 2 (about US$0.05), since Nano Banana keeps them too close to the photo.

cell_options.name: pose
cell_options.label: Pose
cell_options.help: How the birds are painted. A perched bird sits on a plant native to the cell's location when the place is known. Changing the pose paints every bird again, within the daily limit; the earlier paintings stay on the paintings page.

choices.label: Mixed: about a third of the birds in flight

cell_options.name: unpainted
cell_options.label: Until painted
cell_options.help: Show the classic plate or the record's photo while a painting is on its way, or leave the species off the sheet until it is painted, so every picture on the page is in the style.

cell_options.name: when_spent
cell_options.label: When the budget is spent
cell_options.help: Once to-day's painting budget is spent, the species that could not be painted give way to paintings this widget already kept in the same style, cut out like the rest: a different handful each hour, or those on the sheet on the fewest days first. Their labels say when each was last on the sheet, the title line says how many are from the collection, and they are never counted as seen to-day. Nothing is painted for them; one never cut out before is cut once, from the cut-out budget. The cluster and the grid only: a hero and the year list stay as they are.

choices.label: Fill the gaps from the collection, at random
Fill the gaps from the collection, the rarest first

cell_options.name: dapper
cell_options.label: A dapper specimen a day
cell_options.help: One species a day, picked by the date, is painted in a small hat (a top hat, a bowler, a beret, a fez, a crown) in whatever style the sheet is in; its own painting, kept beside the plain one.

cell_options.name: arrangement
cell_options.label: Arrangement
cell_options.help: A scene asks fal.ai to repaint the whole sheet as one picture with one background, once every specimen on it is painted and cut out; until then the sheet shows. One painting per scene, again when the line-up changes.

choices.label: The sheet: each specimen cut out on paper
A scene: the sheet repainted as one picture

cell_options.name: scene
cell_options.label: The scene
cell_options.placeholder: Pick an example, then change the words as you like

presets.label: A Victorian vignette
presets.value: the specimens gathered in an oval cluster, like a Victorian vignette, on branches and foliage that join them

presets.label: One shared branch
presets.value: all perched along one shared branch

presets.label: Through a tree
presets.value: perched through the branches of one tree

presets.label: Round a bird bath
presets.value: gathered round a stone bird bath in a garden

presets.label: Along a wire
presets.value: sitting in a row along a telephone wire against the sky

presets.label: At a feeder
presets.value: gathered at and around a hanging bird feeder

presets.label: In a meadow
presets.value: on the ground and low stems of a wildflower meadow

presets.label: A cottage garden
presets.value: in a cottage garden, on a fence, shrubs and a path

presets.label: The forest floor
presets.value: growing together on a forest floor among leaf litter, moss and a few fallen twigs

presets.label: A wetland edge
presets.value: among reeds and still water at the edge of a wetland

presets.label: In flight
presets.value: all in flight together across an open sky

cell_options.help: Where the specimens are gathered, in your own words. Blank is the Victorian vignette.

choices.label: The model may move and resize the specimens as the scene needs
Every specimen stays where the sheet put it, at its size

cell_options.name: scene_every
cell_options.label: Repaint the scene at most every
cell_options.help: When the line-up changes, the scene is painted again, at about US$0.04 a time, no more often than this.

cell_options.name: refresh_min
cell_options.label: Ask the source every
cell_options.help: GBIF's answer is seasonal and kept for a month regardless.

settings.name: fal_api_key
settings.label: fal.ai API key (clean cut-outs)
settings.help: With a key, every plate and photo on the sheet is cut out by a background-removal model on fal.ai (BiRefNet, well under a cent a picture, once per picture, 300 a day unless you change the cut-out limit below), so a plate with a painted sky or a photo arrives on the page as the specimen alone. Without one, pictures on plain paper are cut by their edges and photos are shown as soft ovals. Get a key at https://fal.ai/dashboard/keys; it is only sent to fal.run.

settings.name: gen_daily_usd
settings.label: Painting budget per day
settings.help: The most the widget may spend on new paintings in a day, at the models' listed prices (US$4 is about a hundred Nano Banana paintings). 0 is no limit. Paintings are kept, so a species in a style only costs once.

settings.name: gen_per_refresh
settings.label: New paintings started per refresh
settings.help: How many new paintings one refresh of a sheet may start (1 to 50). The rest wait for the next refresh, still within the daily number.

settings.name: gen_parallel
settings.label: Paintings made at once
settings.help: How many paintings fal.ai works on side by side (1 to 8). The others wait in the queue on the paintings page.

settings.name: mask_daily_usd
settings.label: Cut-out budget per day
settings.help: Cut-outs (BiRefNet on fal.ai) cost about two cents each. 0 is no limit.

settings.name: mask_per_refresh
settings.label: Cut-outs started per refresh
settings.help: How many new cut-outs one refresh may start (1 to 100).

settings.name: exclude
settings.label: Always leave out
settings.help: Species left off every Specimen Sheet cell, one per line, in the same form as a cell's Leave out list: a name, a genus, a kind or a pattern such as *gull.
